title: Humility that raises
hook: one hadith promises that the way up runs downward

segments.voice: Yesterday, adab with the earth, and your line: plant it anyway. Did something go into the soil, or get watered? Today the path turns from manners to the virtues underneath them. Day one thousand three hundred six.

Where do you sit when you walk into a crowded room? Near the front, where you'll be seen? By the door, where you can slip out? Or wherever's left? Seats say a lot. And one hadith turns the whole question upside down. In Sahih Muslim, in paraphrase, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: no one humbles himself for the sake of Allah, except that Allah raises him. The way up runs downward. Today's virtue, and today's word: tawadu', humility.
screen: `WHERE DO YOU SIT?` → `HUMBLED FOR ALLAH, RAISED BY ALLAH.` → `TAWADU'.`

segments.voice: Notice the small phrase in the middle: for the sake of Allah. This isn't putting yourself down to be noticed, or false modesty fishing for a compliment. It's lowering yourself where Allah sees it, and leaving the raising to Him. The hadith doesn't say how or when. Only who does it. The Qur'an draws the same posture as a way of walking. Surah al-Furqan, in Pickthall's translation: "The (faithful) slaves of the Beneficent are they who walk upon the earth modestly, and when the foolish ones address them answer: Peace." Humility in the feet. And humility in the reply, when someone is rude. Then the reason it matters between people. In Sahih Muslim, in paraphrase, the Prophet said Allah revealed to him: be humble toward one another, so that no one boasts over another, and no one wrongs another. Pride isn't only a private flaw. It's where boasting and wronging start. And what did it look like in a life? Someone asked 'A'ishah what he did at home. Her answer, in Sahih al-Bukhari, in paraphrase: he was in the service of his family, and when the time for prayer came, he went out to pray. And Anas reports, also in Bukhari, that any slave girl of Medina could take the Prophet by the hand and lead him wherever she needed. So tawadu' isn't a mood of feeling small. It's a set of movements: the lower seat, the soft step, the chores at home, the hand that lets itself be taken.
screen: `FOR THE SAKE OF ALLAH, NOT FOR SHOW.` · `AL-FURQAN: WALKING MODESTLY.` · `NO ONE BOASTS, NO ONE WRONGS.` · `IN THE SERVICE OF HIS FAMILY.`

segments.voice: Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind the places you'll sit today: a meeting, a table, a bus, a gathering. Choose one of them. In your mind, take the lower seat there. Let someone else have the better chair, the first word, the credit. Notice what pulls at you when you picture it. Don't argue with it. Just notice. Then picture one chore at home that you usually leave to someone else, and see yourself doing it quietly. If you pray, you can make that small lowering for the sake of Allah. The bell holds the time.
Tawadu'. Humility: lowering yourself for the sake of Allah, in your seat, your step and your service, and leaving the raising to Him. Today's word.
Your line: lowered, raised. Today, take the lower seat once, or do one chore nobody asked you to. Tomorrow, generosity that draws near. Day one thousand three hundred six.

howItsDone: Muslim teaching on tawadu' draws on Qur'an 25:63 and the hadith that no one humbles himself for Allah except that Allah raises him, and on reports of the Prophet serving his family at home.
